caption: A person walking along a pavement catches a foot on a raised kerb, stumbles forward with arms flung out, and recovers balance after two quick steps.

sa.check: A person walks along a pavement.
A foot catches on a raised kerb.
They stumble forward with arms flung out.
They recover balance after quick steps.
The trip comes first, then the stumble, then the recovery.

pc.expect: The stumble begins at the trip.
pc.fail: It begins before; or with no kerb contact; or on flat pavement away from the kerb.

pc.expect: The body pitches forward and the recovery steps are in the direction of travel.
pc.fail: They fall backward; or freeze mid-fall; or step sideways.

pc.expect: They stay on their feet and end upright.
pc.fail: They float; or hover leaning; or sink.

pc.expect: The arms come up at the joints.
pc.fail: They detach; or bend mid-bone; or the body folds mid-torso.

pc.expect: Their limbs keep their number and stay attached.
pc.fail: A limb vanishes; or a second figure appears; or they merge with the kerb.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: Their clothing and the pavement stay the same.
pc.fail: The clothing changes colour; or the kerb moves; or the street rearranges.

note: Biomechanics scene: the body is the physics. Form, posture and skill are not judged; only that limbs stay attached, bend at joints, keep ground contact and pass through nothing.
